In this experiment, we will use the Model 170 Trainer, a pulse width modulator, and a motor driver to demonstrate an open loop, series DC motor.
EXPERIMENT
A voltage source, a Pulse Width Modulator (PWM), an Amplifier/Driver (H-switch), and a motor are the major components in an open loop motor system.
A varying amplitude DC voltage is applied to the PWM circuit, which modulates the width of the pulses.
The current of the pulses is then amplified by the driver circuit and sent to the motor.
As you can see, there is an absence of feedback from the motor to the PWM circuit to account for changes in the operational circuit. This is why the system is considered an "open loop".
There is a relationship between the voltage applied to the motor and its rotational speed. You will notice that as voltage increases, revolutions of the motor (frequency and RPM) will increase...
The measured frequency from the slotted disk attached to the motor is converted into revolutions per minute (RPM).
